title: Coughing over lunch
objective: Monitor the work of assistive personnel and intervene or report when care is unsafe or incomplete
secondaryObjectives: Know that a licensed nurse who delegates keeps accountability for the client and cannot delegate nursing judgment, and that state law decides whether an LPN/VN may delegate to assistive personnel
Assignment and delegation as they apply to the PN, including delegation to assistive personnel

sources.note: Relayed from the REQ-233 NCLEX-PN cases (read 2026-11-11, primary PDF), not re-read: Coordinated Care includes care within the legal scope of practice; Physiological Adaptation includes recognizing and reporting a change in the client's condition.
The objective and secondary objectives are the course's own titles.

brief.situation: 12:10 in a skilled nursing facility. You are the LPN on the east hall. At 12:00 you delegated lunch assistance for Mrs. Kowalski, 84, to Jordan, an agency nursing assistant on a first shift here. Walking past her room, you hear her coughing.
handover: Mrs. Kowalski had a stroke two months ago. Her diet order, from the speech-language pathologist: puréed food, mildly thick liquids, fully upright, small sips.
This state's nurse practice act lets an LPN delegate meal assistance to a nursing assistant; the delegating nurse keeps accountability and supervises.
Facility policy: the LPN reports a resident's change in condition, and any suspected aspiration, to the RN supervisor and the provider at once. The RN supervisor is on the unit.
howItWorks: The clock runs in simulated time; study pace runs three simulated minutes per real minute. Pause any time.
Each check takes the time on its button. Decide what is unsafe, what to do about it within your scope, and who must know.
Partway through you are asked to write your reasoning. A debrief scores what you did.

then.log: Head of the bed at about 30 degrees; Jordan is giving her thin juice from a regular cup between spoonfuls of regular-texture pasta. She coughs after each sip and her voice sounds wet.
Puréed food, mildly thick liquids, fully upright, small sips, supervised meals: from the speech-language pathologist.
'I was told to feed her lunch. No one mentioned thickened drinks; the tray came like this.' Jordan is new and didn't know to report the coughing.

why.question: What is unsafe here, whose responsibility is it, and what do you do?

parts.label: What and whose
parts.criteria: Delegated care not done to the diet order (thin liquids, reclined); coughing and a wet voice are signs of aspiration; the LPN who delegated keeps accountability and must supervise and intervene; the aide was never given the right directions.
parts.modelAnswer: She's being given thin liquids lying back, against her swallow order, and she's coughing with a wet voice: she may be aspirating. I delegated the meal, so I'm still accountable for her, and Jordan never got the right directions.

parts.label: What I do
parts.criteria: Stops the feeding at once and sits her upright; checks her breathing; holds oral intake; reports to the RN supervisor and provider now; gives the aide clear directions and supervises; documents and files an event report.
parts.modelAnswer: Stop the feeding, sit her up and stay with her, check her breathing, and hold anything by mouth. Report to the RN supervisor and provider now. Then give Jordan clear directions and check back on their work, and document it and file an event report.

noProgress.rationale: Suspected aspiration unreported an hour on is harm here.

aspiration.headline: Aspiration
aspiration.body: Delegating a meal does not hand over accountability. Coughing and a wet voice on thin liquids, reclined, against a swallow order means stop now, check her, and report.

caught.headline: Stopped and reported
caught.body: You stopped the unsafe feeding at once, checked her, held oral intake, reported within minutes, and gave the aide the directions they never had. That is the expert path.

caughtGaps.headline: Assessed, with gaps
caughtGaps.body: Check how fast you stopped the feeding and reported, and whether the aide got clear directions.

time_up.headline: Unreported
time_up.body: Suspected aspiration goes to the RN supervisor and provider at once.

scoring.modelReasoning: Mrs. Kowalski's swallow order is puréed food and thick liquids, fully upright. She is being given thin juice reclined, and she coughs after each sip with a wet voice: signs of aspiration. I delegated the meal, so I keep accountability for her and must supervise and intervene; the aide was never given the right directions. Stop the feeding now, sit her upright, clear her mouth and stay, check her breathing, hold anything by mouth, and report to the RN supervisor and provider at once. Then give the aide clear directions, check back on their work, document, and file the event report.
